title: Deconstruction and post-structuralism: why meaning never sits still
examples: What is deconstruction in simple words?
What did Derrida mean by différance?
What is the death of the author?

stages.ask: Is deconstruction the same as saying anything goes?

explain.say: Try this. Look up the word light in a dictionary. It says brightness. Look up brightness. It says radiance. You never reach the end, only more words. In 1966 Jacques Derrida gave a lecture in Baltimore that shook structuralism by pointing at exactly this loop on the board.

explain.say: Follow the cycle. Each meaning sends you to another word, and back again. Derrida called this différance, with an a, which mixes two French senses: to differ and to defer, to put off. Meaning is always on the move. Where do you think it finally stops?

stages.ask: Is deconstruction the same as saying anything goes?

explain.say: Derrida also noticed that Western thought ranks pairs. Look at the left group: speech above writing, presence above absence, reason above madness. Deconstruction shows that the top term secretly depends on the bottom one, and the ranking wobbles. Which pair would you flip first?

draw.name: x-sort
draw.question: Which term does Western thought rank higher?

explain.say: Roland Barthes added a famous essay in 1967 about the death of the author. On the left, the old view: one true meaning, ask what the writer meant. On the right, Barthes: a text is woven from earlier writing, and meaning is made in reading. Does that make you feel freer, or lost?

Here is the exam tip. Deconstruction is not destruction, and it is not anything goes. It is very close reading that finds where a text contradicts itself. Great thinking today. Challenge: find one word in a poem that means two opposite things at once.

faq.a: Derrida's coined word, spelt with an a. It joins the French senses of differing and deferring: a word means only by differing from others, and its full meaning is always put off.
It reads a text closely to find the binary pairs it relies on, then shows how the favoured term depends on the other, so the text's own logic unsettles itself.
asks: How do you deconstruct a text?

faq.a: Derrida's name for the Western habit of treating speech, presence and a fixed centre of meaning as primary, and writing as a lesser copy.

faq.q: What did Barthes mean by the death of the author?
faq.a: That a text's meaning is not locked up in the author's mind. A text is a weave of earlier writing, and its unity lies in the reader, so the birth of the reader costs the death of the author.
asks: What is The Death of the Author about?

faq.q: Is deconstruction the same as saying anything goes?
faq.a: No. Derrida read with great precision. Deconstruction shows that meaning is unstable inside a text, but every claim still has to be argued from the words.
asks: Does deconstruction mean texts mean nothing?

facts: Derrida delivered Structure, Sign and Play at Johns Hopkins University in 1966.
Derrida's Of Grammatology was published in 1967.
Barthes's The Death of the Author first appeared, in English, in 1967.
